name: The deputy of the doer (nāʾib al-fāʿil)
definition: The marfūʿ noun after a verb in the passive, standing where the doer would stand: the one to whom the act was done.
body: When the doer is left out, the verb is put into the passive and the object takes the doer's place and its rafʿ. Al-Ājurrūmiyya calls it 'the object whose doer is not named' (al-mafʿūl alladhī lam yusamma fāʿiluh) and defines it as the marfūʿ noun whose doer is not mentioned with it.

Its verb is recognised by its vowels: in the past the first letter takes ḍamma and the one before the last kasra (ḍuriba), in the present the first letter takes ḍamma and the one before the last fatḥa (yuḍrabu). Like the doer, it is a noun you see or a pronoun.
